# An instance built at run time under a node of a render slot's body is the
# slot's to keep, on every target.
#
# The tabs sit under `if ready`, a slot, and each panel is an instance of its
# own; gtk4 lifts no panel holding a select, so the tabs stay a node of the
# slot's body and the panels instances under it. The slot kept a registry of
# the instances at its body's top and none of these, so a render that dropped
# the About panel built the next and never destroyed the last: its effects
# ran on, and a test still found its `#flavor`. Each is now held, and
# destroyed by the render that builds its replacement.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import test "sngl:test"

component main ui.node {
    var ready = false
    var tab = 0
    var note = "hello"
    var kind = "Red"

    ui.button #load(text="load", @click { ready = true })
    if ready {
        ui.tabs #tabs(:selected=tab) {
            ui.tab(label="About") {
                ui.text #flavor(value=note)
            }
            ui.tab(label="Kinds") {
                ui.select(:value=kind) {
                    ui.choice(label="Red")
                    ui.choice(label="Green")
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

func testSwitchingDropsTheFirstPanel(t test.Test, c main) {
    c.load.click()
    t.assert(c.flavor != null)
    if c.tabs != null {
        c.tabs.change(1)
    }
    t.assert(c.flavor == null)
}
